title: Introduction and Personal Data; Family Background
description: Cathy Naugle begins by recording the basics of the interview setup and asking Brenda Fay Lewis for personal details, including her birth information and phone number. Brenda provides information about her mother's background, parents, siblings, and her marriage to Frank, as well as their blended family of five boys.

title: Frank's Career; Move to Idaho
description: Brenda discusses her husband Frank's extensive career in the grocery business in California, his work issues involving a store in a predominantly black area, and their decision to relocate to Idaho Falls. She recounts how Frank transitioned into the cedar and timber business after moving to Idaho.

title: Children's Details; Education; Skills and Faith
description: Brenda shares the names and birthdates of her children. She then discusses her education, noting she quit school during her sophomore year and later completed her GED. She also talks about her skills, including writing, grocery checking, bartending, craftwork, and how her lifestyle and faith changed after moving to Idaho.

title: Groups and Hobbies; Urban versus Rural Life
description: Brenda mentions her participation in a children's charity Christian group and her hobbies, such as traveling, writing, and reading. She then compares urban and rural living, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages she sees in each, and reflects on how her current family dynamics compare to her own childhood.

title: Recreation; Media; Family Roles
description: Brenda discusses family recreation, such as fishing and other interests, and describes her media preferences, including reading the Bible and watching Mary Tyler Moore. She describes her close working relationship with Frank and how they manage their household and family finances together.

title: Marriage expectations; blended family
description: The interviewer asks how expectations about marriage have changed since before the wedding. The speakers discuss maturity, the adjustments of a second marriage, and the challenges of raising children from two different families together.

title: Empty nest; sons' futures and service
description: The conversation turns to the future, including the prospect of an empty nest when the last child leaves home. The speakers express optimism about their sons, encouraging them toward areas of study, work, and military service as a way to learn a trade and become productive.

title: Marriage as an institution; Christian morality
description: The interviewer asks whether marriage is still a workable institution and how the parents would respond if a son lived with someone unmarried. The speakers ground their views in responsibility before God, biblical teaching, and raising children without a double standard on sexual morality.

title: Sex education dispute at school
description: The speakers recount their objection to sex education classes at school and how they had a daughter removed from the class. They describe writing letters to teachers, the school's response in Saint Mary's, and arrangements for the child to be taught separately.

title: Identity in marriage; moving to rural life
description: The interviewee reflects on whether she lost her identity by always saying 'we' and how she and Frank came together as one. She offers advice to women moving from city to country, describing the year or more it takes to gear down to a slower rural pace.

title: Friendships, faith, and self-acceptance
description: The speakers discuss keeping long-distance friendships alive through letters, including a best friend named Jan, and the strain of separation. The interview closes with the interviewee describing how faith helped her find her identity, stop putting herself down, and begin to like herself.
